_readme: Events added by hand, for programmes no crawler can reach.
WHY: pib.gov.in, meity.gov.in, sih.gov.in, cert-in.org.in and nciipc.gov.in all
refuse requests from data-centre IP ranges, so the GitHub Actions crawl is served
'Access Denied'. National programmes announced only there (Cyber Kushti, Kavach,
the Smart India Hackathon) therefore have to be entered here.
HOW: add an object to 'events' below. Only 'title' is required, but an event with
no startsAt is shown as 'Dates to be announced'. Edit this file on GitHub and the
next crawl picks it up; no code change and no redeploy is needed.
Curated entries are trusted: they skip the relevance filter and may be undated.
If the same event later appears on a crawled source, the two are merged.
Set "published": false to keep a draft here without showing it.

_schema.title: required
_schema.type: "hackathon" or "ctf"; omit to let the classifier decide
_schema.description: a paragraph students can act on
_schema.sourceUrl: where it was announced, e.g. the PIB release
_schema.organizer: e.g. Ministry of Electronics and IT
_schema.startsAt: YYYY-MM-DD or a full ISO timestamp
_schema.scope: "national" (India) or "international"; stated explicitly because the classifier cannot always tell

_example.title: Example National Cyber Security Challenge 2026
_example.description: Replace this block with a real programme. It is here only to show the shape of an entry and is not published, because "published" is false.
_example.organizer: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
_example.eligibility: Students enrolled in an Indian university.
rules: At least one member must be a registered student.

events.title: Smart India Hackathon
events.organizer: Ministry of Education, Government of India
events.description: India's national innovation programme for students of AICTE-affiliated institutions. Ministries, state departments and industry publish problem statements, several of which each edition cover cyber security, digital forensics, drone technology and critical infrastructure. Runs in software and hardware editions with a grand finale at nodal centres. Dates and problem statements are published on the official portal.
events.eligibility: Students of AICTE-affiliated institutions in India, in teams.

events.title: CERT-In programmes and advisories
events.organizer: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), MeitY
events.description: India's national nodal agency for cyber security incident response, under MeitY. Publishes vulnerability advisories and threat intelligence, runs incident response and digital forensics training, and holds periodic national cyber security exercises and challenges. Its site serves a frameset and blocks automated clients, so it is listed here rather than crawled.

events.title: Black Hat
events.description: One of the largest international information security conference series, with Briefings, Trainings and the Arsenal tool showcase. Student rates and associated competitions are announced on the official site. The site blocks automated clients, so it is listed here rather than crawled.

events.title: DEF CON and DEF CON CTF
events.description: The best known hacking conference in the world. Its CTF is among the most prestigious in the field, run by the Nautilus Institute, with open qualifiers ahead of the on-site final. DEF CON also hosts villages covering aerospace, ICS, IoT and car hacking.

events.title: Pwn2Own (Zero Day Initiative)
events.description: The flagship live exploitation contest, with categories spanning browsers, virtualisation, enterprise software, automotive and ICS or SCADA. Targets, rules and cash awards for each edition are published by ZDI.

events.title: Nullcon and Battle Underground CTF
events.description: India's best known international security conference, running training, briefings and the Battle Underground CTF.

events.title: c0c0n
events.organizer: Kerala Police Cyberdome and Society for the Policing of Cyberspace
events.description: An international security conference run in association with Kerala Police, with CTF and hackathon tracks and a strong law-enforcement and digital-forensics focus.

events.title: InCTF
events.description: A long-running Indian student capture the flag, with a national junior edition and an international edition. Covers binary exploitation, reverse engineering, web, cryptography and forensics.
events.eligibility: Junior edition is for school and undergraduate students in India.

events.title: CSAW
events.description: One of the largest student-run security events, with qualifier and final rounds and a dedicated India region hosted at IIT Kanpur.
events.eligibility: Student teams; regional finals are open to qualifying teams.

events.title: Hack In The Box
events.description: International security conference series running deeply technical briefings and the HITB CTF.

events.title: Google CTF
events.description: Google's annual capture the flag, with a qualifier open to everyone and a Beginners Quest aimed at newcomers.

events.title: SANS Holiday Hack Challenge
events.description: A free annual challenge from SANS, deliberately beginner friendly and a good first CTF. Stays open for several weeks and covers a broad range of security skills.
events.eligibility: Open to everyone, free to enter.

events.title: Hack The Box competitions
events.description: Runs the Business CTF, a University CTF for student teams, and continuous practice labs. Useful for building a team before entering a rated event.
